With reference to the attached communication from the
Netherlands Consulate-General dated September 30, 1935, on the
subject of Kniazeff, a ballet dancer, I have to state that
Nicholas Alexeevitch Kniazeff, Russian, was born on May 10, 1907
at Novocherkask, Don Province.
Up to 1925 he resided at Moscow, where he studied at the
Ballet School of Elliroff, a ballet master of the Moscow Government
Theater.
In 1925 Kniazeff came to Harbin together with Elliroff's
ballet troupe, as Elliroff's personal secretary, where he stayed
until 1926 when the troupe came to Shanghai.
Whilst in Shanghai, Kniazeff, being a very good ballet
dancer, made his appearance in various ball-rooms and in 1927
left for Manila, Netherland's Dutch Indies and Egypt, travelling with the
Cherpine's ballet troupe.
He returned to Shanghai from the tour in March 1929 and
in September of the same year left for Java, being engaged there
for one season.
From 1931 up to present Kniazeff has been engaged as a
ballet master at the "International Cafe" in Hankow.
He is duly registered with the Russian Emigrants' Committee
118/1 Moulmein Road, as a Russian emigrant.
There is nothing in Municipal Police records to his
detriment.

日期：1936年10月15日。
事由：荷兰总领事馆关于俄国人克尼亚泽夫（Kniazeff）的来函。
由 D.S. 马卡罗夫（Makaroff）呈报，经 D.S.S. 洛约（Loyau）转呈

关于随附的荷兰总领事馆1935年9月30日就芭蕾舞演员克尼亚泽夫一事发出的信函，本人谨陈述如下：尼古拉·阿列克谢耶维奇·克尼亚泽夫（Nicholas Alexeevitch Kniazeff），俄国人，1907年5月10日出生于顿河省新切尔卡斯克（Novocherkask）。
1925年之前，他居住在莫斯科，在莫斯科政府剧院芭蕾大师埃利罗夫（Elliroff）的芭蕾学校学习。
1925年，克尼亚泽夫作为埃利罗夫的私人秘书，随埃利罗夫芭蕾舞团来到哈尔滨，并在那里停留至1926年，随后该团来到上海。
在上海期间，克尼亚泽夫作为一名优秀的芭蕾舞演员，曾在各舞厅登台演出，并于1927年随谢尔皮内（Cherpine）芭蕾舞团前往马尼拉、荷属东印度和埃及旅行演出。
他于1929年3月结束巡演回到上海，同年9月前往爪哇，在那里受聘演出一季。
从1931年至今，克尼亚泽夫一直受聘担任汉口“国际咖啡馆”（International Cafe）的芭蕾指导。
他已作为俄国流亡者在莫尔海姆路118/1号的俄国流亡者委员会正式登记。
工部局警务处档案中没有任何对他不利的记录。

With reference to attached letter dated July 16,

23 years of age, ballet dancer by profession, and performs under

in May 1929 and since that time has been working as a ballet
dancer in local theatres etc..

she is engaged to be married to a British subject named Francis
Dudley Fursland .

formerly connected with the Volsky troupe (File D. 506), nothing
is known in this office against her.

G. Prokofiev

a member of his ballet in July 1930
which was planning to proceed to Soerabain.

application for passport facilities was refused
by the local Netherlands' Authorities on the
ground that he was reputed to be an auxiliary
agent of the Comintern.

SHANGHAI, 20th May 1930.

Sir,

I wish to refer to my letters of 14th September 1929, No. 7705
and 2nd June 1929, and to that of 10th September No. I. C. D.
505 concerning amongst others the following couple "Kinzeff".

I have now come to Shanghai for a short time and desire to
transmit them to Netherlands India in company of :

1. Mr Alexander Stefanovich Deviatkin (whose name alias is Kinzeff),
born at Tula 17 December 1896, living at 9 North Honan Road, at
present employed at the Little Club, and possessing a passport
issued by the Commissioner of Foreign Affairs at Shanghai on
25th March 1929, No. 754.

2. Mrs. Elizabeth Feodora Tchernichkina, whose husband disappeared
about 10 years ago, born at Orel (U. S. S. R.) 11 December 1902,
living at the same address as Mr Deviatkin and also employed
at the Little Club. The number of her passport is 155.

I gather from Mr. Kinzeff's statements that he is not related
to a certain Kinzeff, who was Soviet Commercial Attache in Harbin,
but would be grateful to have this confirmed, if possible, by you.
His present address is at 9 North Honan Road.

I would be much obliged to hear from you whether there is
anything known against these persons either from moral or political
point of view.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,

Consul-General.
